blog_summary: Adrian Colyer highlights AI2 as a novel approach that combines human intelligence (HI) with artificial intelligence (AI) to improve cybersecurity threat detection. The system uses an ensemble of unsupervised learning models (PCA, Replicator Neural Networks, and copula functions) to identify suspicious events, which are then reviewed by human analysts. The human feedback is used to train a supervised model, creating a feedback loop that refines future detections. This hybrid approach significantly reduces false positives compared to pure unsupervised learning while detecting a higher percentage of attacks. The paper demonstrates that with a daily investigation budget of 200 events, AI2 detects 86.8% of attacks with a 4.4% false positive rate, outperforming unsupervised-only methods.
paper_title: AI2: Training a big data machine to defend
paper_venue: IEEE International Conference on Big Data Security
